propositions: The deterministic readiness floor admitted ticket classical-grey-ayeaye (fd6b-09c5-8f76-45ad) with a PASS+signature verdict despite P1 and P10 blocking findings present in det_advisory, while identically-shaped sibling tickets (545a-4db5-3a64-42d9 and 0d3c-ff25-5317-4d73) were blocked by the same floor in the same review window.

The bug-tier branch in plan_review_precheck downgraded all DET findings except P4 from det_blocking to det_advisory before the LLM tier, allowing P1/P10 floor violations to be bypassed for ordinary bug tickets while task siblings retained those blocks and short-circuited to BLOCK.

A signed plan-review attestation lacking objective acceptance criteria violates the documented deterministic-floor contract and breaks the claim gate's downstream assumption that reviewed plans have verifiable criteria.

Direct runtime calls to det_floor.run_det_floor over the three pre-rewrite bare descriptions all produced P1+P10 blocks, confirming the floor itself is deterministic; the divergent PASS verdict for the bug fixture originates in workflow_ops.py's bug-tier downgrade, not nondeterministic parsing or model sampling.

At least 15 other signed attestations in the store were minted over plans lacking acceptance criteria (carrying DET P1 findings in their review results), requiring re-review before their PASS verdicts can be trusted for claim/close decisions.
